correctness.rationale: Conditional on K=k moved labels, the ordered prefix is a uniform injection and the fixed suffix consists exactly of the labels above its maximum M. For M>k, condition also on the position of M: the k−1 other positions form a uniform injection into [M−1], and the k−1 distinct target labels are in [M−1]. A common relabeling of the targets and alphabet identifies its fixed-count law with the stated partial-injection law. At M=k the prefix is a full permutation. For a t-entry injection into [m], the factorial moments are (t)_s/(m)_s; termwise product comparison with (t/m)^s and absolutely summable factorial-moment inversion yield the e²/t bound. The geometric hazard comparison includes the last survival test j=n−k, at which survival is zero. Replacing the conditional Poisson parameter by k/n costs at most (j+2)/n, and the endpoint M=k costs at most 1/n for k<n. For k=n the full-permutation bound applies directly. The occupancy mean differs from a by O_c(n⁻¹) and its variance is O(n⁻¹) by nonpositive indicator covariances. The uniformly bounded second ℓ¹ derivative of the convolution on [a/2,1], the signed average of the linear term, and Chebyshev on k<an/2 give the claimed rate for fixed c>0. The nested checker and output were inspected, not run; the proof does not use the finite data.

value.rationale: The estimate quantifies an explicitly identified convergence-rate question for a natural critical-time statistic. It improves on simply conditioning and bounding deviations absolutely by showing why fluctuations of order n⁻¹/² contribute only order n⁻¹ to this distribution. This yields a finite-size error guarantee for all fixed-point events, not just selected moments.
